name: Mystery setting
summary: A method that sets cut stones on a hidden rail so that no metal shows between them and the stones form one surface.
how: Cut each stone with a groove on its sides.
Slide the stones on thin metal rails inside a frame.
Close the frame so that no claw or prong shows.

origin.note: Van Cleef and Arpels patent the mystery setting, with stones of one colour on a hidden rail.

adoptions.via: Paris houses set rubies and sapphires so that no metal shows between the stones in flat Art Deco clips.
Small mystery-set rubies make the spray of colour at the centre of a gold bow.
